senses.gloss:
Bhūman
(‘the Great one’)
------------------------------------------
The उपनिषद्स् are the main sources of the Vedānta philosophy which has gained a pre-eminent place, in इन्दिअन् फिलोसोफ्य् superseding the other systems.
One of the most important subjects discussed by the उपनिषद्स् is ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute, the origin and substratum of this created universe.
Out of the several terms used in the उपनिषद्स् to designate ब्रह्मन् the word ‘Bhūman’ or ‘Bhūmā’ is an uncommon one, used only in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.23-25). Literally, it means ‘that which is very big or great’.
Nārada, the well-known sage of the पुराणस्, approaches Sanatkumāra, the great teacher of his times, and begs him for instruction regarding the आत्मन् or the Self, the knowledge of which alone can give freedom from sorrow.
Sanatkumāra teaches him the techniques of a graded meditation, the objects chosen for the same varying from nāma or name up to प्राण or the vital energy responsible for life. In this series Bhūmān comes last. When this भूमन् is experienced, one attains supreme joy, compared to which all the pleasures of life pale into insignificance.
This भूमन् is not only everywhere and in everything, it is also our inner Self. One who realizes this becomes ‘svarāḍ,’ ruler of his own self. He also attains the freedom to move in all the regions of this universe.
This section of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad is known as Bhūmavidyā.
